title: Services
objectives: Differentiate foreground, background and bound services
Choose the right tool for long-running work

sections.markdown: A Service is an app component for work without a UI. It does NOT create its own thread — long work must run on a background thread or it blocks the main thread.
Assuming a Service runs on a background thread. It runs on the main thread by default — do heavy work on a worker thread/coroutine, or you'll get ANRs.

Since Android 8 (Oreo), background services are restricted to save battery. For deferrable/guaranteed work use **WorkManager**; for ongoing user-visible work use a **foreground service** with a notification.
Don't reach for a Service by default. For most background tasks, WorkManager or coroutines are the right answer; reserve services for truly ongoing work (music, navigation, location).

flashcards.front: Does a Service run on a background thread?
flashcards.back: No — it runs on the main thread by default; you must offload heavy work yourself.
Foreground shows a persistent notification for user-visible work; background is short and restricted since Android 8.

flashcards.front: Modern choice for guaranteed deferrable work?

quiz.q: A Service by default runs on…
quiz.explain: Services share the main thread; offload heavy work explicitly.
Foreground services must show an ongoing notification.

quiz.q: For guaranteed deferrable background work, use…
quiz.explain: WorkManager handles constraints, retries and survives reboots.
